column16: Applicants to the Smeal One-Year MAcc Program must have an undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. Prerequisites include: Financial Accounting, Managerial Accounting, Intermediate Accounting I, Intermediate Accounting II, Cost Accounting, Introduction to Taxation, and Auditing. Non-native English speakers must also provide proof of English proficiency.
column47: The Penn State Smeal Master of Accounting (MAcc) Program offers two paths to a graduate degree and the 150 credit hours required to be a CPA: The Integrated MAcc Program and the One-Year MAcc Program. The program provides the specialized knowledge and professional skills needed for success in the accounting profession, preparing students for the challenges of the profession and meeting the requirements for CPA licensure in most states. Smeal accounting graduates are highly sought after by top accounting firms and corporations, gaining technical knowledge necessary for success in public accounting, corporate accounting, and other related fields.

column2: Master of Science in Accounting Analytics

column38: Penn State Smeal College of Business
column47: The Penn State Smeal College of Business is merging its two one-year accounting master’s programs — the Master of Science in Accounting Analytics (MAA) and the Master of Accounting (MAcc) — to create a single, comprehensive program: the Master of Science in Accounting Analytics. Starting in fall 2024, the new MAA curriculum will integrate coursework focused on data analytics and technology skills with traditional accounting courses. The curriculum is designed to equip students with the necessary skills to navigate the evolving landscape of the accounting profession and meet the increasing demand for professionals with expertise in data-driven decision-making. The program will offer one-year master’s students two paths to CPA licensure: a non-business path for students with a non-accounting background and an accounting path for those with a bachelor’s degree in accounting. As part of the program, students will participate in a three-credit immersion experience, working in teams to address a real-world accounting analytics problem. They also will gain exposure to emerging technologies like blockchain, artificial intelligence and robotic process automation. The MAA program is STEM-designated and prepares students for the CPA exam.

The program provides a unique opportunity for students to learn about the entire AM process, from design to production, and gain hands-on experience with the latest AM technologies. Students integrate graduate-level coursework across multiple departments including mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, engineering science and mechanics, and materials science and engineering to provide a holistic view of the AM industry. All students in the M.Eng. degree program must complete a capstone project (3 credits) as their culminating experience, which provides the opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills they have gained throughout the program to a real-world AM problem.

column47: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) degree is a non-thesis professional degree that can be earned through the Penn State World Campus or in residence. This program is designed to provide students with the necessary background for a career in the nuclear industry or in a national laboratory. Nuclear engineering is a multi-disciplinary field with many types of career opportunities. Nuclear engineers can work on the development of nuclear power plants for large-scale electricity generation, or for propulsion of submarines, ships and spacecraft. Nuclear engineers also apply nuclear radiation and isotopes in medicine, such as in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer. They also apply these same techniques in industry for the inspection of materials and the development of new materials. Some nuclear engineers work on the development of nuclear-fusion-based power plants. Other nuclear engineers specialize in the nuclear fuel cycle, including the mining, processing and enrichment of uranium, the design and fabrication of nuclear fuel, the management of spent fuel, and the disposal of radioactive waste.

column47: The Graduate Certificate in Additive Manufacturing and Design program is designed to educate students and working engineers in the analytical and practical methods for the design and manufacturing of devices utilizing additive manufacturing. Additive manufacturing (AM) is a suite of emerging technologies that fabricate three-dimensional objects directly from digital models through the repeated addition of material. AM provides a new design paradigm, allowing for the creation of components with unprecedented levels of complexity and/or parts that are produced locally and on-demand. The program is designed to provide students with a foundational knowledge in the entire AM workflow, including the design, materials, and processing of AM parts. The program is a multidisciplinary program with faculty from the College of Engineering and the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences. As such, the program provides a unique opportunity to integrate various aspects of AM, including design, and the materials and processing of AM parts, to ensure students are provided with the most comprehensive AM education.

Students in the certificate program will learn the basics of clinical research, including the design and conduct of clinical trials, the analysis of clinical data, and the ethics of clinical research. They will also learn about the regulatory process for the development of new medical treatments and the translation of basic research into clinical practice.
